 Aday Mara 
 OKC 
 Center 
 #15 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Aday Mara delivered a season-high 18 points (8-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and three blocks over 27 minutes in a one-sided win over the Wizards on Saturday.
 Mara made the most of his opportunity to start on the second night of a back-to-back and was able to exploit Washington’s injury-depleted interior defense on the offensive end of the floor while also pulling down eight boards. The 21-year-old rookie figures to see plenty of action this upcoming week with the Thunder set to play four times, including back-to-back tilts against the Trail Blazers before facing the Clippers and Kings. He’s worthy of a roster spot in most fantasy leagues based on his ability to impact the defensive end of the floor. He’s averaging 8.1 points, 5.9 rebounds, 1.3 assists and 1.9 blocks through 10 games this season. That’ll work.
 -  George Bissell

 Jaylin Williams (back) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Williams will miss a fifth straight game while dealing with lower-back spasms. Aday Mara’s playing time has increased recently, and that should be the case on Wednesday as well.

 Guard 
 #3 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Kenrich Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Tuesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder made one change to their starting lineup, with McCain replacing Aday Mara. Portland has only one true big in its lineup, Donovan Clingan, so starting two 7-footers wouldn’t have been the best course of action.

 OKC 
 Center 
 #15 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Saturday’s game against the Wizards. 
 The Thunder will start Saturday’s game with a bigger lineup, with Mara starting and Jared McCain coming off the bench. While the production hasn’t been consistent, Mara is worth the risk due to injuries to Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren. 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #2 
 The Oklahoma City Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 The Thunder are going smaller in this game than they did against the Cavs with Aday Mara heads to the bench and Jared McCain returns to the starting lineup. Mara will go back to being a backup center while McCain might get more minutes in this game. If McCain is available, he might be worth grabbing if you need some points and 3’s.

 Jaylin Williams (back) has been ruled out against the Grizzlies on Friday. 
 Williams will miss a second straight game, which may result in another start for Aday Mara. However, Mara got the nod against the Cavaliers, who start both Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. Mark Daigneault may opt for a smaller starting unit against Memphis.

 The lone change to the lineup that started Monday’s win over the Cavaliers is Mara, who replaces Jaylin Williams. The 7-foot-3 rookie is making his first career start.

 #15 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Although Jared McCain is available for Monday’s game, the Thunder are starting with a bigger lineup. JayWill has replaced him, which should help the Thunder match up better against Cleveland’s Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. 
 Isaiah Hartenstein 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #55 
 Isaiah Hartenstein amassed 10 points (3-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds and three steals in Saturday’s loss to the Rockets. 
 With Chet Holmgren (knee) out for at least 8-10 weeks, the Thunder will rely even more on Hartenstein, Jaylin Williams (3/4/1/1) and Aday Mara (seven points, nine rebounds, three assists and four blocks) in the post. Of the three, Hartenstein is the safest option for fantasy managers, which is why he’s rostered in over 80 percent of Yahoo leagues. 
 Chet Holmgren 
 OKC 
 Center-Forward 
 #7 
 According to ESPN’s Tim MacMahon, Chet Holmgren (knee) will be sidelined for at least 8-10 weeks. 
 According to MacMahon, Holmgren underwent a biological treatment on Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear in his right knee. With Jalen Williams (ankle/fibula) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) facing extended absences, and given Holmgren’s injury history, fantasy managers should expect the Thunder to be very cautious with his rehab process. Kenrich Williams should remain in the starting lineup for the foreseeable future, and Aday Mara’s playing time should increase. Also, Holmgren’s absence raises Isaiah Hartenstein’s fantasy ceiling. 
 Jaylin Williams 
 OKC 
 Forward 
 #6 
 Jaylin Williams (wrist) will not return to Sunday’s game against the Clippers. 
 JayWill played five minutes off the bench before leaving with a sore right wrist, and the Thunder have now shut him down for the rest of the night. His exit will likely result in more playing time for fellow reserve Aday Mara, who logged seven minutes in the first half.

 Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 25 points (9-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets.
 Lendeborg has scored at least 25 points in six games this season. Against the Rockets, he shouldered more of the offensive workload after Stephen Curry (core) exited, finishing with his third double-double. Through 12 games, only Wilt Chamberlain and Rick Barry have scored more points as a rookie in Warriors history than Lendeborg. The Warriors visit the Spurs on Friday in what will be another challenging matchup for Yaxel, especially if Curry can’t play.

 Fred VanVleet finished Wednesday’s win over the Warriors with 18 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, three steals and four three-pointers.
 “Steady Freddie” has been the calming influence the Rockets lacked last season while he was recovering from an ACL tear. Against the Warriors, VanVleet shot 66.7 percent from the field and posted solid numbers in assists, steals and three-pointers. VanVleet is currently providing top-100 fantasy value, and that’s closer to his floor than his ceiling.

 Amen Thompson recorded 19 points (8-of-11 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal and two blocks in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors.
 Thompson remains a valuable fantasy option, especially for managers willing to punt three-pointers. However, his scoring average has decreased by more than three points per game compared to last season. Thompson’s ability to fill a stat line has preserved most of his value.  Durant led six Rockets in double figures on Wednesday, and he’s scored at least 20 points in four straight games. Given his career résumé, that isn’t a significant achievement for KD.  Darryn Peterson got himself 22 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, and two 3-pointers in 123-108 loss to the Magic. 
 Over the past week, Darryn Peterson has gotten more confident, aggressive, and the Jazz have been letting him lose. The peripheral stats from college have started to come back, and it’s been exciting to watch. You want more in terms of efficiency, but with Lauri Markkanen out for a month, Darryn is a must roster if he hasn’t been picked up in your league already.

 Ace Bailey has been great this season and has been one of the best shot blockers in the NBA. His ability to havoc defender at this point is a great sign for his long-term development.
